memory.interpretation: Strong immediate state dependence plus additional long-history information. The prior 3.5-year claim is superseded; the tested optimum is 10 years and nearby long-memory candidates are similar.

quantitative_state.model: within-transect fixed effects; cyclic survey-day and log sampled-point-count adjustment; node-cluster bootstrap
quantitative_state.interpretation: Recorded presence and quantitative meadow condition are partly decoupled. This is a candidate cryptic-degradation/state-decoupling result, not yet an environmental-causal result.

pulse_2016_2017.survey_date_warning: 24/47 eligible 2016 visits use 2016-12-25; four of five pulse nodes use this date.
pulse_2016_2017.effort_warning: Pulse-node 2016/2015 sampled-point ratios range from 0.854 to 3.545.
pulse_2016_2017.date_semantics_warning: Pinned OBIS conversion uses minimum date within IDall, while current tbeptools read_formtransect uses maximum date for multi-day samples.

claim_boundary: Do not equate recorded presence/non-detection with demographic occupancy/extinction.
Do not interpret the 2016/2017 pulse as a confirmed ecological disturbance until original survey-date/protocol semantics are resolved.
Braun-Blanquet values are ordinal abundance classes, not percent cover.
Blade length and shoot density are secondary because measurement coverage is incomplete.
Current environmental associations are descriptive; no climate-causal attribution is supported.
Do not select a nominal annual water-quality association as a mechanism after inspecting the screen; no declared post-2016 association survives FDR control.
Do not add further retrospective seasonal windows to rescue the hot/fresh mechanism; both annual and predeclared 3/6-month screens are negative.

lower_tampa_bay.interpretation: Consistent with compositional reorganization toward more frequent Halodule while Thalassia and Syringodium decline quantitatively; not proof of competition or replacement mechanism.

old_tampa_bay.interpretation: No strong monotone alternative-seagrass replacement; the stronger signal remains declining Thalassia blade length and shoot density.

middle_tampa_bay.interpretation: Thalassia and Syringodium year-to-year frequency changes are positively rather than negatively coupled; the stronger focal signal is declining Thalassia blade length.

community_reorganization.synthesis: Post-2016 degradation mode differs among bay segments rather than following one common Tampa-wide trajectory.

environmental_coupling.interpretation: No simple annual water-quality variable currently provides a multiplicity-controlled segment-year explanation of post-2016 state changes. Environmental causation remains unresolved; finer-scale stress mechanisms remain possible.

exposures: maximum monthly mean temperature over prior 3/6 months
minimum monthly mean salinity over prior 3/6 months
seasonal_hot_fresh_screen.interpretation: Aligning hot/fresh exposure to 3- and 6-month pre-survey windows does not recover a multiplicity-controlled association with Thalassia frequency or Braun-Blanquet state change. Acute/finer-scale mechanisms remain unresolved.
